review.limitations: Expository review, not independent verification of the constructions it cites. Statements about subgroup knowledge and computing resources are historical to this article.

evidence.description: Four complementary descriptions of the Monster

sections.title: What it explains
sections.text: Borcherds introduces the Monster through finite groups, representations and algebraic structures it preserves.

sections.title: The organizing idea
sections.text: Knowing a group’s size gives less structural understanding than realizing it as automorphisms of an algebra. The article presents the Griess algebra, Monster vertex algebra and Monster Lie algebra as complementary perspectives.

sections.title: How the explanation develops
sections.text: The exposition follows numerical clues into graded representations and then trace series. Vertex-algebra structure and a no-ghost construction connect those series to Lie-algebra denominator identities.

sections.title: The motivating clue
sections.text: The equality 196884=196883+1 connects a modular-function coefficient with representation dimensions. It motivates moonshine but is not, by itself, its proof.

sections.title: Conclusion and limits
sections.text: The Monster vertex algebra provides a particularly informative realization. Borcherds nevertheless finds its construction conceptually unsatisfying. The short article sketches explanations; it does not reproduce their full proofs.
